name: Acetylene generator
description: A steel tank that makes low-pressure acetylene from water and calcium carbide, with a gauge and an outlet valve for a torch hose.
notes: A water tank 180 mm across with a domed gas bell, a carbide hopper cap, a gauge on the front, a brass outlet valve and a carry handle, 400 mm tall. CHECK VOLUME (x5.9): the reference's 3 L is far below any tank that holds a working charge of water; the handle and valve also stand off the tank. acetylene_supply is a new quality name for feeding a cutting or welding torch; the reference lists none. Charging it with water and carbide needs fuel content that does not exist yet.

name: Pallet of dry adobe bricks
description: A light wooden pallet carrying fifteen sun-dried mud bricks, hard and ready to build with.
notes: Fifteen bricks 220 by 140 by 80 mm in three rows on a three-stringer pallet 1.22 m long. Box volume is 1.9 times the reference because the pallet's open frame and the gaps between bricks count as air. brick-buff stands in for pale dry earth. Taking it apart into bricks and the pallet has no content field yet, and Deadvox has no adobe brick item. The wet pallet is its own model because drying is a distinct state. The size is a placeholder for a thing too large for a pack.

name: Pallet of wet adobe bricks
description: A light wooden pallet carrying fifteen freshly moulded mud bricks, still soft and drying.
notes: The dry pallet's shape with clay-wet bricks and the heavier wet mass. It is made by the player, never found, so it has no spawn tiers. Drying into the dry pallet over a week needs timed item transformation, which has no content field yet. The size is a placeholder.

name: Angle grinder
description: A mains power tool with a fast abrasive wheel under a half guard, for cutting and grinding metal. It has a screw-in side handle.
notes: A 115 mm grinder 0.42 m long lying on its wheel, side handle on +z. CHECK VOLUME (x4.0): the side handle and the wheel stand off the slim body. Qualities are metal_cutting 2, the powered grade, and sharpening, under names other drafts use; the reference lists none. It needs mains power, which Deadvox tools have no field for yet.

name: Bench vice
description: A heavy cast-iron vice on a swivel base, with a small anvil flat behind the fixed jaw. It is meant to be bolted to a bench.
notes: A 100 mm vice 408 mm from the anvil flat to the tommy bar, screw to the front on +z. CHECK VOLUME (x24): the reference's 0.75 L is about the iron alone (5.4 kg at cast-iron density); the box counts the air between jaws, slide and base. clamping and anvil follow the reference's qualities; clamping is a new quality name, 2 for a bench vise, and the clamp in this batch has 1. Bolting it down as a workstation needs a placed-furniture form, so it is drafted as a carried tool.

name: Tongue-and-groove pliers
description: Large slip-joint pliers with angled jaws that set to several widths. They grip pipes and nuts.
notes: The pliers family's groove kind at 300 mm, jaws open. wrenching follows the reference's wrench quality under the name the base content uses.

name: Block and tackle
description: Two steel pulley blocks with hooks, reeved with rope, for lifting a heavy load by hand.
notes: Two triple-sheave blocks laid flat and pulled apart, three falls of rope between them and the free end trailing; 0.40 m overall. Box volume is 3.2 times the reference because the falls leave air between the blocks. hoisting is a new quality name; jacking is kept for lifting vehicles. The reference category is spare parts; it is drafted as a tool because it brings a quality.

name: Wooden block and tackle
description: Two wooden pulley blocks in rope strops, reeved with rope, for lifting a load by hand. Less sturdy than steel.
notes: Two double-sheave blocks with rope eyes in place of hooks, two falls and a trailing free end; 0.44 m overall. CHECK VOLUME (x4.6): the falls leave air between the blocks; 0.4 L would be the blocks alone. The sheaves show as a dark mortise in each shell. hoisting 1 against the steel set's 2 for its weaker frame.

name: Brick kiln
description: A portable sheet-steel kiln on short legs, fired with coal or charcoal, for firing bricks and other clay.
notes: A firebox 380 by 320 by 310 mm with a latched door and a draught slide on the front, a capped flue at the back of the roof and two side handles; 0.61 m tall with the flue. Box volume is 3.2 times the reference because the flue stands well above the box. firing is the quality name for kilns that fire clay, apart from charring. Burning coal or charcoal needs fuel content that does not exist yet.

name: Bronze pickaxe
description: A cast bronze pickaxe head on a long wooden handle, with a pointed pick for breaking rock and a flat wedge for prying it loose.
notes: A 0.9 m walnut-toned handle with a 470 mm head, laid flat. CHECK VOLUME (x6.4): the head's T shape leaves most of its box empty. digging and mining stand in for the reference's mining use; mining is a new quality name. It would also swing as a heavy weapon; that weapon block is left to the base content's melee tuning.

name: Carding paddles
description: A pair of wooden hand carders faced with fine wire teeth, for combing raw wool or fibre straight before spinning.
notes: Two paddles 265 mm long laid side by side, teeth up, each a 150 by 100 mm board with a leather card cloth and sixteen rows of teeth. Box volume is 2.7 times the reference because the pair leaves air between the handles. carding is a new quality name; the reference lists none. leather-tan draws the card cloth.

name: Paint chipper
description: A stiff steel scraper blade on a short wooden handle, for chipping old paint and rust off a surface.
notes: A 50 mm blade in a brass ferrule on a 100 mm handle, 176 mm overall. CHECK LENGTH (x3.5): the reference's 50 mm longest side matches the blade's width, not a tool with a handle; its 300 mL volume fits the whole scraper. scraping is a new quality name; the reference lists none.

name: C-clamp
description: A cast steel C-shaped clamp with a screw and swivel pad, for holding work pieces together.
notes: A 100 mm clamp lying flat, its frame 150 mm tall, screw opened with the tommy bar out past the frame. clamping follows the reference's quality, shared with the bench vice in this batch.

name: Claw bar
description: A short steel pry bar with a flat chisel end and a curved split claw for pulling nails. Also a weapon.
notes: A 240 mm hexagonal bar with the gooseneck claw rising at +x and its split painted dark. Qualities follow the reference under base content names; its nail-prying quality is covered by prying. It would swing as a light blunt weapon like the crowbar; that weapon block is left to the base content's melee tuning.

name: Concrete mixer
description: A portable electric concrete mixer: a plastic drum on a geared yoke with a tilt wheel, on a two-wheeled stand with push handles.
notes: Modelled standing ready to load, drum mouth up, 1.30 m from the wheels to the handles. CHECK VOLUME (x4.9): the reference's 250 L counts it folded; the box counts the open stand and handles. The reference's folded state would need its own model and an unfold action, which has no content field yet; one standing model keeps it recognisable. mixing is a new quality name; the reference's container quality is left to the item's container block. It needs mains power, which Deadvox tools have no field for yet. It is too large for a pack, so the size is a placeholder; as a set-down machine it may later suit a workstation.
